prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for everyone — the right choice depends on your needs (budget, roof type and size, whether the job is insurance-related, desired warranty, timeline, etc.). I can help you find the best contractor for your situation. To start, answer any of these or tell me what matters most to you:

- Your Dallas ZIP code or neighborhood
- Residential or commercial roof?
- Roof material you want (asphalt/fiberglass shingles, architectural shingles, metal, tile, TPO, etc.)
- Is this a storm/insurance claim or a homeowner-pay job?
- Any budget or timeline constraints?

While you decide, here’s a practical guide to pick the best Dallas roofing company and what to expect.

How to identify top roofing companies
- Look at Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor and local Facebook groups; prioritize companies with many recent positive reviews.
- Verify insurance: they should carry general liability and workers’ compensation (or show proof of payroll if they don’t carry WC).
- Ask about licensing and local registrations (some cities or municipalities require roofer registration/permits).
- Check manufacturer credentials: are they certified for the shingle/roof system you want? Certification often affects warranty.
- Request references for recent similar jobs and, if possible, drive by completed roofs.

Top questions to ask every contractor
1. Are you licensed/registered to work in Dallas and do you pull permits?
2. Can you provide proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp?
3. How long have you been in business locally?
4. Do you have manufacturer certification for the product I want?
5. What’s included in your bid (tear-off, number of layers, disposal, deck repair, flashing, vent upgrades)?
6. What warranties do you offer (manufacturer vs workmanship, transferability)?
7. Who will supervise the job, and what is the projected timeline?
8. Will you provide a written contract and final lien waiver?
9. How do you handle unexpected deck damage or hidden issues?
10. Can you provide references and photos of recent similar jobs?

What should be in the written contract
- Detailed scope: materials (brand, model, color), number of layers to be removed, underlayment, ventilation, flashing details
- Start and completion dates
- Total cost and payment schedule (avoid full upfront payments)
- Permit responsibilities and inspection plan
- Warranty details and claim process
- Disposal of old materials and site cleanup

Red flags to avoid
- Very low bids that seem too good to be true
- Contractor asks for full payment upfront
- No physical business address or poor/no online presence
- Refuses to provide insurance certificates or written contract
- High-pressure sales tactics (e.g., demand to sign today)

Typical costs and timeline (Dallas, ballpark)
- Costs vary widely by roof size, slope, complexity, and materials. A typical asphalt shingle replacement on a modest single-family home often ranges broadly (several thousand to tens of thousands). Get at least 3 written estimates for accurate comparison.
- Most replacements take 1–3 days of work for an average house once started, plus permit/inspection timing.

If you want, I can:
- Prepare a short email/phone script you can use to contact contractors
- Make a recommended checklist you print for on-site estimates
- Help assemble a short list of Dallas-area roofers if you give your ZIP and job details
